title: Explain a Workshop Proposal

source.rights: 原创 AI 辅助虚构教学材料；尚待独立教学与发音审核。

instructions: Prepare briefly and record your own response of 120–160 words. The sample is shorter than the 90–120 second target. Add relevant details and allow natural pauses while staying within 120–160 words.
prompt: Speak for about 90–120 seconds, using 120–160 words. Describe a fictional workshop proposal, compare two options, and explain a concern and a planned next step. Use at least six lesson words.
reference: I would propose a small community workshop where neighbors make a picture together. The aim is to share ideas and enjoy the process, not to create a perfect artwork. One option is to show the work on a table, and another is to put it on a board. The board has an advantage because it can leave more room for visitors to move. My concern is whether it can stand safely in the chosen place. The organizer is meeting the building manager on Friday, and we will decide after that conversation. A designer could draw a prototype with a pencil and use glue for a sample label. I would divide the tasks so one person prepares a leaflet while another checks the calendar. If we use photography, we will ask each participant before sharing a recognizable picture. This approach gives everyone a way to contribute.
